This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.38/2024 dated 18.01.2024 registered at Police Station Sihora, District Jabalpur for the offences punishable under Section 420, 120-B, 186 and 34 of IPC.

2. Learned senior counsel for the applicant contends that the present applicant is working as Computer Operator and in identical allegation which has been levelled by the prosecution not only the present applicant but against the co-accused Om Prakash Agrawal who has already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated 09.02.2024 passed in M.Cr.c.No.5719/2024.

It is contended by the senior counsel that the allegations against the applicant is that the rice paddy Nitesh Kumar Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189933967/
1 procured from the farmers though initially was kept in godown but later on, kept in an open place and got mixed.

sentences.text: The rice paddy was also not protected and on account of heavy rain, the same got deteriorated.
Therefore, the offence under the aforesaid Sections has been registered.
It is contended by the senior counsel that as there was no attempt to deceive by the applicant, the ingredients of Section 415 of IPC were not made out.
Therefore, the allegations levelled against the applicant even if taken into consideration in their entirety, they do not constitute commission of aforesaid offence.
It is further contended by the senior counsel that the applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation and trial.
Therefore, the applicant be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the application and submitted that the paddy was kept in open place which was procured from different farmers and got mixed,
therefore, it was difficult to distinguish the quantity of rice paddy which were supplied by the respective farmers and moreover as the rice paddy was kept in open place and no measures were taken to protect the same, the rice paddy was deteriorated after heavy rain, therefore, he is not entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

5. Heard the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

It is evident from perusal of record that the allegations against the applicant was that he kept the rice paddy in open place upon procuring it from farmers and the same got deteriorated on account of heavy rain.

Co-accused Om Prakash Agrawal has already been enlarged on anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 09.02.2024 passed in M.Cr.c.No.5719/2024.
7.

Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, prima facie the applicability of Section 415 of IPC is a debatable issue, thus, this Court deem it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant namely Nitesh Kumar Patel shall be enlarged on bail on furnishing a personal bond in a sum o f Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before him during the course of investigation or before the trial Court during trial, as the case may be.

9. It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by all the conditions as enumerated under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
